Premature ejaculation A universally accepted definition of premature ejaculation has not yet been established, but the American Urological Association has defined it as ejaculation that occurs sooner than desired, either before or shortly after penetration, causing distress to either one or both partners.1 Management may include psychological, behavioural, and drug treatment.1 Several antidepressants have been evalu- ated for a therapeutic effect in premature ejaculation,1-3 based on their adverse effects of anorgasmia and delayed ejaculation. The SSRIs fluoxetine, paroxetine, and sertra- line, and the tricyclic antidepressant clomipramine, have been used successfully. However, the optimal dosing regi- men for these drugs has not been established, and they have been given either on a continuous daily basis or as single doses only before intercourse. Doses that have been effective in premature ejaculation have usually been lower than those recommended for the treatment of depression. A rapidly absorbed short-acting SSRI, dapoxetine, is un- der development specifically for on-demand treatment of premature ejaculation.
